title: Quickstart
text: Quickstart Install the published package for your language. Native Node, Python and .NET packages currently include Windows x86, x64 and ARM64 libraries. Rust can build from source; browser WASM is independent of the host CPU architecture. Download a GGUF supported by the selected llama.cpp build, then pass its local path. Terminal Copy python -m pip install --upgrade turbojev npm install @turbojev/node dotnet add package TurboJev cargo add turbojev cargo add turbojev-runtime-llamacpp --features ffi quickstart.py Copy from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("./model.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192, n_seq_max=1) as jev: response = jev.evaluate( { "state": "My package arrived broken. Please send a replacement.", "questions": { "team": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this?", "criteria": { "billing": "Charges and refunds", "shipping": "Delivery, damage and replacements", "technical": "Software and service outages", }, }, }, } ) print(response["answers"]["team"]) evaluate returns decisions in answers . generate returns typed scalar and structured fields in result . Neither promises that the selected model will interpret every question correctly. Start with clear instructions and measure your own cases. Repository samples Samples exercise this checkout and build its local artifacts. The separate demos repository installs published packages; each Python demo owns its code and data. PowerShell · repository root Copy py samples/build.py native --arch x64 py samples/run.py python --model C:/models/model.gguf py samples/run.py ts --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate py samples/run.py csharp --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate py samples/build.py web py samples/run.py web Choose one architecture supported by your build toolchain: x86 , x64 , or arm64 . From inside samples/ , use py build.py and py run.py , without repeating the directory.

title: Architecture
text: Architecture The core accepts evaluate requests for typed decisions and generate requests for scalar workflows. It validates dependencies, conditions, nullable values and workload limits. An adapter renders the model's real prompt and tokenizer, returns candidate scores, and lets TurboJev validate, normalize, calibrate, and build the response. state text · JSON · media → questions / fields choice · noul · score · scalars → TurboJev core plan · score · respond → typed response answers / result + skipped Core owns Schema, candidate and dependency validation Execution planning and calibration metadata Typed responses, conditional omissions and scalar validation Order robustness and parity contracts Adapters own Chat template and tokenizer GGUF, Transformers.js, or custom runtime Media preprocessing and hardware Process, file, and network boundaries

title: Core API
text: Core API Operation Request Result evaluate State and choice/noul/score questions answers : typed decisions generate Context and typed fields or an object schema result , skipped , usage : extraction and workflows evaluateCompatible Compatibility profile and evaluation request Profile-specific response Choice, boolean decision and ordered score Canonical request Copy { "state": "Everything is down and our biggest client has a demo at noon.", "questions": { "urgent": { "type": "noul", "instructions": "Does this need a reply within the hour?" }, "team": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this?", "criteria": { "outage": "Service down", "billing": "Charges and refunds", "feature": "Requests and how-to" } }, "tone": { "type": "score", "instructions": "How upset is the customer?", "criteria": ["calm", "annoyed", "furious"] } } } choice selects a semantic key and returns its relative probability distribution. Exact ties select the lexicographically smallest key. noul returns a boolean-decision probability; boolean is an input alias. score returns the expected zero-based index: sum(index × probability) . Its criterion order defines the scale; changing that order changes the meaning. Finite decisions versus generated fields Use generate for strings, integers, numbers, nullable values, finite enums, dependencies and conditional fields. Finite fields score candidates; open strings and numbers generate bounded tokens. A numeric enum is an unordered choice, not an ordered score. Candidate probabilities are conditional on the supplied options, not calibrated confidence. Option ordering explains the default single pass and optional corrections. Decision design explains prompt construction, legal actions and testing.

title: Typed fields
text: Typed fields Structured SDK extensions describe source version 0.32.0, awaiting publication. Build this revision to use the new APIs; registry demos retain published packages. generate adds JSON-typed fields to TurboJev's portable core. evaluate remains the direct choice , noul and ordered score API. Finite fields score model candidates; unrestricted strings and numbers generate a bounded value. Extraction therefore generates tokens and can take longer than a single candidate decision. Request and response python Copy Structured SDK extensions describe source version 0.32.0, awaiting publication. Build this revision to use the new APIs; registry demos retain published packages. from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("invoice.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192, n_seq_max=1) as client: response = client.generate( context="Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions={ "total": {"type": "number", "instructions": "What is the total in GBP?"}, "overdue": {"type": "boolean", "instructions": "Is payment overdue?"}, "reminder": { "type": "string", "when": {"overdue": True}, "depends_on": ["total"], "instructions": "Write one short payment reminder.", }, }, thinking=False, text_max_tokens=128, numeric_max_tokens=64, ) print(response["result"]) print(response["skipped"], response["usage"]) The same JSON request is accepted by every binding. Supply exactly one of questions (a field map) or schema (an object with properties , optional required , and optional additionalProperties: false ). All declared properties are requested; required validates property names, not a separate omission policy. Conditions control omissions. The schema subset supports scalars, nested objects and top-level arrays; nested arrays and arrays inside objects are rejected. Exact finite-value ties compare JSON value encodings; probabilities are not rounded into artificial ties. state is an input alias for context . Field option Behavior type string , integer , number , boolean , or [type, "null"] ; retains JSON types enum 1–512 unique values of that type; a singleton is a constant with no model scoring instructions / description Question; description is the fallback depends_on Names of earlier results to include as plain values; forward references allowed when AND of tests on prior fields; adds implicit dependencies return_probabilities Boolean, finite fields only; returns a value/confidence/distribution wrapper permutations Finite booleans/enums: positive integer, auto , or all thinking Per-field override: false, true, or auto thinking_effort none , low (512 tokens), medium (2048), high (4096) thinking_budget Positive token budget, up to 32768; alternative to effort Token limits are request-level text_max_tokens (default 256) and numeric_max_tokens (default 64), each 1–32768. Booleans default to [true, false] , plus actual null for nullable booleans. Numeric equality distinguishes booleans from integers and does not round distinct 64-bit integer values. Unsupported keywords, including bounds, string length/format constraints and unsupported container combinations, are rejected before inference rather than ignored. Invalid generated output and exhausted budgets are errors. Wllama 3.8.1 exposes top-N vocabulary scores and its Jinja autoparser does not apply custom GBNF on this path. The adapter resolves letter labels through the loaded model tokenizer using textual logit-bias keys, applies the same additive offset to every permitted label, and requests post-sampling probabilities with truncation disabled. A common offset preserves candidate log-odds and the conditional distribution; it does not favor the first option or select a winner. This uses one model call for 2–26 candidates. Missing or invalid scores are errors, never invented probabilities. The browser adapter does not claim a selective output head. Objects, arrays and scales Object leaves use scoped dependency names and return the original nested shape. Top-level arrays accept scalars or grammar-constrained objects. They support minItems, maxItems and continue_from; without a maximum, each call can append at most 50 new items. Duplicates stop deterministic extraction; sampling permits two retries. The model supplies every item. structured.json Copy { "context": "Ada is 37 years old and says she is furious.", "questions": { "person": { "type": "object", "properties": { "name": { "type": "string" }, "age": { "type": "integer" } } }, "tone": { "type": "number", "levels": [ { "label": "calm" }, { "label": "annoyed" }, { "label": "furious" } ], "return_probabilities": true } } } Described choices use choices: [{value, description}] instead of enum. A number field with 2–26 ordered levels returns the expected zero-based level. It cannot be permuted. Large text enums (27–512) need complete continuation scoring: native GGUF and ONNX implement it; GGUF/WASM requires an explicit value-scorer plugin. They have a higher cost than one-token decisions. See the cookbook for dense pages, large category sets, hierarchical routing and category discovery. Dependencies, conditions and null Dependencies form a validated acyclic graph. A dependent prompt receives only its named previous answers, without probability wrappers. The media envelope and its bytes stay intact. Fields currently execute serially in dependency order; this API does not promise shared-prefix batching or parallel field generation. Response fields return in caller order. json Copy { "context": "The account has seven overdue invoices.", "questions": { "count": { "type": "integer", "instructions": "How many invoices?" }, "escalate": { "type": "boolean", "when": { "count": { "gte": 5 } }, "instructions": "Should support escalate this account?" }, "reference": { "type": ["string", "null"], "instructions": "Return the payment reference, or null when it is absent." } } } Tests support equality, list membership, and objects with in , not_in , ne , gt , gte , lt , lte . Comparison operands are type-checked. Open string fields may be tested for null, but not arbitrary string equality. A false condition skips the field and all its dependents without inference, including automatic effort selection. Skipped fields are absent from result and named in skipped ; they are not invented null answers. Actual null is present in result . The string "null" stays a string. Probabilities and permutation budgets json Copy { "type": "string", "enum": ["heads", "tails"], "instructions": "Which side of a fair coin will appear?", "permutations": "all", "return_probabilities": true } The result wrapper contains value , confidence , probabilities and distribution . distribution is an array of {value, probability} retaining actual JSON types. Map keys normally use string values or JSON spellings for other scalars. In nullable string enums, the literal string "null" uses the quoted map key "\"null\"" to distinguish it from actual null's "null" key. Prefer the typed array if keys matter. Each ordering receives a real model evaluation. Scores are normalized separately, remapped to original values, then probabilities are averaged. auto uses canonical ordering and a Williams design: N evaluations for an even N, 2N for an odd N greater than one. Integer budgets sample distinct orderings reproducibly using request seed ; the identity is included. all visits every permutation. A hard cap of 720 prevents accidental factorial workloads. A six-sided die with all costs 720 evaluations; opt in deliberately. Averaging may reduce position bias but does not guarantee correct reasoning or calibrated confidence. This policy is separate from evaluate 's load-time none , cyclic and balanced policies. Positive integer budgets include the caller listing and are not generally order invariant; use auto for canonical layouts. Numeric enums are unordered, unlike score . See option ordering . Confidence, sampling and SDK helpers Probability output defaults to permutations: "auto" for small unordered fields unless a budget is explicit. Set permutations: 1 for one pass. Large enums and ordinal scales default to one pass. The wrapper separates raw selected probability from confidence . Choice confidence measures the top probability above uniform; ordinal confidence measures dispersion around the modal level. Neither is fitted calibration. A when confidence gate uses numeric bounds in 0–1 and requires probability output on its parent. Request temperature defaults to 0. Positive temperature samples finite decisions using seed . Native GGUF supports seeded open values; the ONNX adapter explicitly rejects that open-value mode. Python adds Choice , compiled Decision / ArrayField , Generation / Usage , compile_json_schema , candidate_softmax , run_schema , example_schema , encode_image and benchmark_prefix_cache . Node exports model-free compileJsonSchema and candidateSoftmax . C# adds CompileSchema , CandidateSoftmax and typed GenerateAsync . C/WASM expose JSON compiler/normalizer functions. Existing JSON methods remain available. Python generation accepts a timeout or a thread-safe GenerationControl . Node/browser accept {timeoutMs, signal} ; C# accepts TimeSpan and CancellationToken . Cancellation is cooperative before/after model operations; an active decode must finish. Browser workers serialize requests and process cancellation messages separately. The optional images request accepts up to 32 encoded images in order. Python encodes bytes, paths, data URIs or PIL-like objects; browser imageEvidence encodes Blobs. Load a compatible vision model plus projector. URLs are fetched explicitly by the application. Thinking and runtime capabilities Default generate thinking is false, independently of the load-time policy used by evaluate . A field can override the request. Budget-only field overrides inherit the request's on/off setting. Effort selects the setting explicitly. Contradictory settings fail validation. auto asks the model to choose none/low/medium/high as an additional hidden finite decision, exposes that selection in thinking_effort , and then performs the actual field request. It cannot also specify a fixed effort or budget. Runtime Finite fields Text/numbers Reasoning Native llama.cpp/GGUF Candidate logits JSON grammar plus Rust type checks Bounded text-model reasoning using the model's actual template Browser llama.cpp/WASM Candidate log probabilities JSON Schema grammar plus Rust type checks Explicit unsupported error Transformers.js text Token logits Bounded greedy generation, validated afterward; no grammar mask Explicit unsupported error Existing custom scorer/fixture Finite scoring Requires implementing infer_field / inferField Requires that hook Native and browser GGUF field generation accept the existing image/audio/video-frame envelope when the loaded model and matching projector support the modality. That is not a promise of receipt-reading accuracy. Native media reasoning is explicitly unsupported. Video inputs are decoded, timestamped image frames; TurboJev does not decode video containers or invoke external media executables. Current published native binaries cover Windows x86/x64/ARM64; portable source and WASM support do not imply Linux/macOS binary releases or execution on every architecture. usage.decisions counts completed output fields, not hidden effort queries or permutation evaluations. input_tokens sums known actual model counts; generated_tokens counts actual generated reasoning/value tokens. thinking contains actual model reasoning where supported. Increase context and reduce nSeqMax for longer reasoning. Unsupported modes, context overflow and unfinished reasoning return errors; no fallback answer is fabricated. Binding calls Language Method Rust engine.generate(GenerateRequest) ; types in turbojev::schema::fields Python client.generate(request) or client.generate(context=..., questions=...) Node/TypeScript await client.generate(request) ; exported GenerateRequest / GenerateResponse Browser await client.generate(request) or await wasmEngine.generate_json(JSON.stringify(request)) .NET await engine.GenerateJsonAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(request)) C tj_engine_generate_json(handle, json, &output) then tj_string_free(output) Android engine.generate(JSONObject(request)) Swift try engine.generate(json) on its managed affinity thread The native ABI is shim version 10; rebuild native dependents together. Runtime options are scoped to each field and restored after errors. Native nSeqMax=1 uses independent reference scoring for multiple questions. Shared-prefix reuse needs at least two sequences; parallel suffix reuse needs at least three. Scheduling changes do not switch the configured CPU/GPU device. Existing evaluate requests and responses remain supported. Tests and evals adapted from TypeLLM Reference tests TurboJev coverage Schema, nullable, grammar fields, text Scalar and enum typing, duplicate/invalid values, null wire presence, bounded native grammar generation Dependencies, conditions Forward references, cycles, typed operators, plain prior values, skipped descendants, skipped auto effort, media-envelope preservation Permutations, probabilities Unique seeded samples, Williams positions/neighbours, normalization and probability averaging, typed null distribution Thinking Validated flags, efforts and budgets, actual hidden effort calls, runtime errors rather than fabricated reasoning Images Existing media contracts plus field-generation path; model accuracy is measured separately Batching, concurrency, prefill, serving protocols Existing TurboJev worker/affinity and runtime tests remain; TypeLLM's SGLang-specific batching, remote-server and logprob-transport tests are not claimed as implemented here Run cargo test --workspace --locked and the browser runtime tests. evals/run.py records real numeric and JevBench model quality, errors, provenance and latency. TypeLLM's numeric cases and the three example ports have attribution and licenses; its published model results are not reused as TurboJev evidence. Decoding and diagnostics Generate accepts mode (argmax or sample), temperature, seed and numeric_max_digits (default 32). Positive temperature alone enables sampling; explicit argmax stays greedy. Level distributions use level names. Failed generation retains reported usage. The Dice cookbook recipe includes sampling, numeric limits and runtime-specific prompt diagnostics.

title: Cookbook
text: Cookbook These workflows adapt all four articles in the TypeLLM cookbook to local inference. Use a model suited to the evidence and decision: typed output does not guarantee accuracy. This structured SDK extension is a source change awaiting publication; build this revision for new APIs. Registry demos retain the last published packages. Extract a dense page in batches Use a vision GGUF and its matching projector. The model supplies rows and the continuation decision; host code only enforces a bounded loop and stops when no progress is made. python Copy from pathlib import Path from turbojev import TurboJev rows = [] with TurboJev.load("vision.gguf", mmproj="mmproj.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192) as client: for _ in range(10): response = client.generate( context="Extract every invoice line in reading order. Never repeat existing rows.", images=[Path("invoice.png")], text_max_tokens=512, questions={ "rows": { "type": "array", "instructions": "Return the next invoice lines, then stop when none remain.", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "description": {"type": "string"}, "quantity": {"type": "integer"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}, }, }, "continue_from": rows, }, "has_next": { "type": "boolean", "depends_on": ["rows"], "instructions": "Are any printed invoice rows still absent from rows?", }, }, ) next_rows = response["result"]["rows"] advanced = len(next_rows) > len(rows) rows = next_rows if not response["result"]["has_next"] or not advanced: break print(rows) Without a maximum, each call can append 50 new items. An explicit maxItems instead limits the total array, including its prefix, to 1–50. Each object is actual constrained generation; this is not single-token classification. The model and context limit determine usable page complexity. More than 255 categories Schemas accept up to 512 typed values. Native GGUF and text ONNX compare complete value continuations for more than 26 values, with the complete set in the prompt. python Copy from turbojev import TurboJev categories = [f"category_{index}" for index in range(418)] with TurboJev.load("model.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192) as client: response = client.generate( context="The document explicitly identifies category_17.", questions={ "category": { "type": "string", "enum": categories, "instructions": "Which exact category is stated?", "return_probabilities": True, "permutations": 1, } }, ) print(response["result"]["category"]) Replace identifiers with meaningful application categories/descriptions. This shows the API, not measured 418-class accuracy. GGUF/WASM requires a value-scorer plugin and otherwise errors. A large enum has a higher prompt/scoring cost; comparing only its first tokens is incorrect. Hierarchical classification Choose a department, then ask only its category. Unchosen branches appear in skipped and are absent from the result. Probability wrappers are unwrapped in dependent prompts. python Copy from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("model.gguf", device="cpu") as client: response = client.generate( context="I was charged twice and want a refund.", questions={ "department": { "type": "string", "enum": ["billing", "technical"], "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", }, "billing_category": { "type": "string", "enum": ["refund", "invoice", "payment_method"], "instructions": "What billing issue is described?", "when": {"department": "billing"}, }, "technical_category": { "type": "string", "enum": ["login", "outage", "performance"], "instructions": "What technical issue is described?", "when": {"department": "technical"}, }, }, ) print(response["result"], response["skipped"]) The described-choice/confidence variant is in hierarchical.json . Discover and reuse categories Offer current categories plus new . Only if selected, ask for a category name. The application reviews and stores the proposal; TurboJev does not mutate its taxonomy. python Copy from turbojev import TurboJev categories = ["groceries", "transport", "utilities"] with TurboJev.load("model.gguf", device="cpu") as client: response = client.generate( context="Receipt: dog grooming, 45.00.", questions={ "category": { "type": "string", "enum": [*categories, "new"], "instructions": "Choose an existing expense category, or new if none fits.", }, "new_category": { "type": "string", "instructions": "Propose a short reusable expense category name.", "when": {"category": "new"}, }, }, ) print(response["result"]) Inspect the contract without loading a model python Copy from turbojev import Choice, compile_json_schema schema = { "type": "object", "properties": { "team": Choice("Which team?", {"billing": "Payments", "outage": "Service down"}).to_schema() }, } for decision in compile_json_schema(schema): print(decision.name, decision.choices) Compilation runs Rust validation. The metadata contains semantic values rather than unchecked model-specific token IDs. Generation still validates each request. Select latency and cancellation deliberately Set permutations: 1 for one finite evaluation. Probability requests without a budget default to balanced layouts for small unordered fields. Ordered levels remain single-pass. python Copy from turbojev import GenerationCancelled, GenerationControl, GenerationTimeout, TurboJev with TurboJev.load("model.gguf", device="cpu") as client: control = GenerationControl(timeout=30) try: response = client.generate( context="The service is down.", questions={"outage": {"type": "boolean", "permutations": 1}}, control=control, ) print(response["result"]) except GenerationCancelled: print("Cancelled between model operations") except GenerationTimeout: print("Deadline expired between model operations") Another thread may call control.cancel() . Native cancellation does not interrupt an active decode; it aborts the workflow after that operation. Node/browser use client.generate(request, {timeoutMs: 30000, signal}) ; C# accepts TimeSpan and CancellationToken . An aborted workflow is not a model-selected null answer. Fair die: measure the model distribution The Dice helper builds a six-face enum. TurboJev scores the model's answers and samples from its returned probabilities. It never makes the distribution uniform. from turbojev import Dice, TurboJev with TurboJev.load("Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf") as client: response = client.generate( context="A single roll of a fair die.", questions={"roll": Dice(permutations="auto").to_schema()}, mode="sample", temperature=1, seed=42, ) print(response["result"]["roll"]) One permutation is one pass; auto uses six layouts; all uses 720. Report timing and divergence from 1/6 per face instead of claiming that a model is a fair RNG. Decoding controls Argmax is the default. Positive temperature alone enables sampling. Sample mode without temperature uses 1; sample with zero is invalid. Explicit argmax stays greedy even with positive temperature. Ordered levels return their expected index and probabilities keyed by level names. Numeric extraction Set numeric_max_digits (default 32) to limit digits across integer and fractional parts. Native GGUF constrains decoding; every adapter validates the returned value. Numeric enum constants are exempt. Wllama may override custom grammar during Jinja processing, so WASM also enforces the contract after inference. Failures and diagnostics Generation errors retain reported token usage. Native GGUF and ONNX can return formatted prompts when print_final_prompt is true. GGUF/WASM rejects that flag because its runtime does not expose the final prompt.

title: Rust
text: Rust Native, strongly typed integration with the crates directly. crates.io ↗ Cargo.toml Copy [dependencies] turbojev = "0.31" serde_json = "1" turbojev-runtime-llamacpp = { version = "0.31", features = ["ffi"] } Make a decision main.rs Copy use turbojev::TurboJev; use turbojev_runtime_llamacpp::{ffi::{FfiLlamaCpp, NativeConfig}, reference_backend, ReferencePromptConfig, ReferencePromptRenderer}; fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let runtime = FfiLlamaCpp::open("./model.gguf", NativeConfig::default())?; let renderer = ReferencePromptRenderer::new(ReferencePromptConfig::new( "my-app-v1", "Choose exactly one allowed code.", "Which team should handle this?")); let engine = TurboJev::new(reference_backend(renderer, runtime)); let request = turbojev::schema::EvaluationRequest { model: None, state: serde_json::json!({"message": "My package arrived broken."}), questions: [("department".to_owned(), turbojev::schema::Question::choice( "Which department should handle this?", [("billing".to_owned(), "Payments".to_owned()), ("shipping".to_owned(), "Delivery".to_owned()), ("other".to_owned(), "Other".to_owned())].into_iter().collect(), ))].into_iter().collect(), }; let answer = engine.evaluate(request)?; println!("{:?}", answer.answers); Ok(()) } Runnable source: samples/TurboJev-rust ↗ Generate typed fields Deserialize a portable request into the exported scalar workflow type. Use the same engine as above. fields.rs Copy let request: turbojev::schema::fields::GenerateRequest = serde_json::from_value( serde_json::json!({ "context": "Invoice total: 324.50 GBP.", "questions": { "total": {"type": "number", "instructions": "What is the total in GBP?"}, "currency": {"type": "string", "enum": ["GBP", "USD", "EUR"], "instructions": "Which currency?", "permutations": "auto", "return_probabilities": true} }, "thinking": false, "numeric_max_tokens": 64 }) )?; let response = engine.generate(request)?; println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&response)?); Choice correction is configured with engine.with_order_robustness(turbojev::OrderRobustness::Balanced) . Ordered score scales remain in caller order. See option ordering .

title: Node / TypeScript
text: Node / TypeScript Worker-backed native calls with typed results and clean async shutdown. npm ↗ npm install @turbojev/node Copy decision.ts Copy import { TurboJev } from "@turbojev/node"; const jev = await TurboJev.load({ model: "./model.gguf", nGpuLayers: 0, nThreads: 4 }); try { const result = await jev.evaluate({ state: { message: "My package arrived broken." }, questions: { department: { type: "choice", instructions: "Which department should handle this?", criteria: { billing: "Payments", shipping: "Delivery", technical: "Product issue", other: "Other", }, }, }, }); console.log(result.answers.department); } finally { await jev.close(); } Text and media source: TS sample ↗ Evaluate an image Load a supported vision GGUF and its matching projector. Both are inputs to the same native host; no external Python worker is required on this path. load-media.ts Copy const engine = await TurboJev.load({ model: "./vision-model.gguf", mmproj: "./matching-mmproj.gguf", device: "cpu", nCtx: 8192, nSeqMax: 1, }); Once the engine is configured with that runtime, pass the same media envelope to evaluate : media.ts Copy import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"; const result = await engine.evaluate({ state: { contract: "turbojev.media.v1", modality: "image", base64: (await readFile("photo.jpg")).toString("base64"), }, questions: { scene: { type: "choice", instructions: "What animal is shown?", criteria: { cat: "A cat", dog: "A dog" }, }, }, }); console.log(result.answers.scene); Generate typed fields Call inside the same engine lifecycle shown above. A skipped field is absent; it is not a null value. fields.ts Copy const response = await jev.generate({ context: "Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions: { total: { type: "number", instructions: "What is the total in GBP?" }, overdue: { type: "boolean", instructions: "Is payment overdue?" }, reminder: { type: "string", when: { overdue: true }, depends_on: ["total"], instructions: "Write one short payment reminder.", }, }, thinking: false, text_max_tokens: 128, numeric_max_tokens: 64, }); console.log(response.result, response.skipped, response.usage); For unordered routing, configure execution: {orderRobustness: "balanced"} at load time. For finite generated fields, use their own permutations setting. See all field options and ordering costs .

title: Python
text: Python A context-managed API that returns ordinary dictionaries. PyPI ↗ pip install turbojev Copy decision.py Copy from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("./model.gguf", n_gpu_layers=0) as jev: result = jev.evaluate( { "state": {"message": "My package arrived broken."}, "questions": { "department": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": { "billing": "Payments", "shipping": "Delivery", "technical": "Product issue", "other": "Other", }, } }, } )["answers"]["department"] print(result["choice"]) print(result["probabilities"]) Runnable source: samples/TurboJev-Python ↗ Generate typed fields fields.py Copy with TurboJev.load("./model.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192, n_seq_max=1) as jev: response = jev.generate( context="Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions={ "total": {"type": "number", "instructions": "What is the total in GBP?"}, "overdue": {"type": "boolean", "instructions": "Is payment overdue?"}, "reminder": { "type": "string", "when": {"overdue": True}, "depends_on": ["total"], "instructions": "Write one short payment reminder.", }, }, thinking=False, text_max_tokens=128, numeric_max_tokens=64, ) print(response["result"], response["skipped"], response["usage"]) Python accepts a request dictionary or keyword arguments for generate . Load options use snake_case; nested execution options retain JSON spelling: execution={"orderRobustness": "balanced"} . See nullable values, conditions and thinking .

title: C ABI
text: C ABI Stable UTF-8 JSON ABI for C, Zig, Go, and other FFI hosts. header ↗ smoke.c Copy #include "turbojev.h" #include <stdio.h> int main(void) { tj_engine *engine = NULL; if (tj_engine_open_json("{\"model\":\"./model.gguf\"}", &engine) != TJ_OK) return 1; char *json = NULL; const char *request = "{\"state\":{\"message\":\"My package arrived broken.\"},\"questions\":{\"route\":{\"type\":\"choice\",\"instructions\":\"Which team?\",\"criteria\":{\"billing\":\"Payments\",\"shipping\":\"Delivery\"}}}}"; int rc = tj_engine_evaluate_json(engine, request, &json); if (rc == TJ_OK) { puts(json); tj_string_free(json); } tj_engine_close(engine); return rc != TJ_OK; } The ABI uses opaque handles, explicit string ownership, and thread-local errors. Generate typed fields Use the same handle and ownership rules as evaluation. fields.c Copy const char *fields = "{\"context\":\"Invoice total: 324.50 GBP.\"," "\"questions\":{\"total\":{\"type\":\"number\"," "\"instructions\":\"What is the total in GBP?\"}},\"thinking\":false}"; char *output = NULL; int status = tj_engine_generate_json(engine, fields, &output); if (status == TJ_OK) { puts(output); tj_string_free(output); } The shim ABI is version 10. Build C dependencies against matching libraries. Load JSON accepts execution.orderRobustness ; generated fields accept the options described under typed fields .

title: .NET / C#
text: .NET / C# NuGet package with native assets for three Windows architectures. NuGet ↗ dotnet add package TurboJev Copy Program.cs Copy using TurboJev; using System.Text.Json; await using var jev = await TurboJevEngine.LoadAsync(new { model = "./model.gguf", nGpuLayers = 0, nThreads = 4 }); var request = new { state = new { message = "My package arrived broken" }, questions = new { department = new { type = "choice", instructions = "Which department?", criteria = new { billing = "Payments", shipping = "Delivery", technical = "Product issue", other = "Other" } } } }; var json = await jev.EvaluateJsonAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(request)); Console.WriteLine(json); The package carries win-x86, win-x64, and win-arm64 native assets. Evaluate an image Load a supported vision GGUF and its matching projector before sending image evidence. LoadMedia.cs Copy await using var engine = await TurboJevEngine.LoadAsync(new { model = "./vision-model.gguf", mmproj = "./matching-mmproj.gguf", device = "cpu", nCtx = 8192, nSeqMax = 1 }); With a multimodal engine, serialize the portable request and call EvaluateJsonAsync : Media.cs Copy using System.Text.Json; var request = new { state = new { contract = "turbojev.media.v1", modality = "image", base64 = Convert.ToBase64String( await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("photo.jpg")), }, questions = new { scene = new { type = "choice", instructions = "What animal is shown?", criteria = new { cat = "A cat", dog = "A dog" }, }, }, }; Console.WriteLine(await engine.EvaluateJsonAsync( JsonSerializer.Serialize(request))); Generate typed fields Use the loaded engine and serialize the same portable request. Fields.cs Copy var fields = new { context = "Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions = new { total = new { type = "number", instructions = "What is the total in GBP?" }, overdue = new { type = "boolean", instructions = "Is payment overdue?" }, reminder = new { type = "string", when = new { overdue = true }, depends_on = new[] { "total" }, instructions = "Write one short payment reminder." } }, thinking = false, text_max_tokens = 128, numeric_max_tokens = 64 }; Console.WriteLine(await jev.GenerateJsonAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(fields))); Load-time choice correction uses execution = new { orderRobustness = "balanced" } . Generated field enums use permutations independently. See field options .

title: Browser / WASM
text: Browser / WASM Run locally in a web worker with optional WebGPU. npm ↗ npm install @turbojev/web @turbojev/wasm @turbojev/runtime-llamacpp-wasm Copy app.ts Copy import { TurboJevWeb } from "@turbojev/web"; const jev = await TurboJevWeb.load({ model: "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF", wasmModuleUrl: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@turbojev/wasm@0.31.0/turbojev_wasm.js", runtimeModuleUrl: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@turbojev/runtime-llamacpp-wasm@0.31.0/src/index.js", runtimeOptions: { device: "wasm", modelUrl: "https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF/resolve/23749fefcc72300e3a2ad315e1317431b06b590a/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf", }, orderRobustness: "none", // Optional: "cyclic" or "balanced" (extra evaluations) }); const result = await jev.evaluate({ state: { message: "My package never arrived" }, questions: { route: { type: "choice", instructions: "Choose a team", criteria: { billing: "Billing", shipping: "Shipping", support: "Support" }, }, }, }); console.log(result.answers.route); await jev.close(); Included vanilla studio: python samples/build.py web . Try the browser playground The playground runs real inference in a worker. Select the input type before loading a model. Unload the current model to change it. Downloads start only when you press Load. Model selection Input Models Method Text · ONNX Qwen2.5 0.5B, Qwen3 0.6B Transformers.js candidate-token logits Text · GGUF Qwen3 0.6B Q8_0 llama.cpp WASM constrained-answer log-probabilities Image CLIP B/32, CLIP B/16 Image–text similarity Image · GGUF LFM2-VL 450M Q4_0 + mmproj llama.cpp WASM mtmd image input Audio CLAP HTSAT Sound–text similarity Audio · GGUF LFM2 Audio 1.5B Q8_0 + mmproj Wllama mtmd audio input; real Node/WASM probe passed, browser qualification pending Video CLIP or LFM2-VL GGUF Four ordered, timestamped frames; no audio track Media limits Files must be at most 24 MB. Audio is mixed to mono at 48 kHz and must be 10 seconds or shorter. Video must be 60 seconds or shorter; the llama.cpp path sends four ordered, timestamped frames to mtmd. This does not guarantee temporal understanding and ignores the audio track. Small models can return incorrect decisions. Runtime assets The package supplies the worker bridge. The example uses matching published 0.31.0 WASM and GGUF adapter assets from jsDelivr. Use a bundler that emits the package worker on your own origin; if serving plain HTML, host the package worker locally and set workerUrl . You can host the WASM and adapter assets yourself instead. The repository includes Transformers.js and llama.cpp WASM adapters. The llama.cpp adapter loads a matching mmproj for supported image models and passes video as ordered, timestamped image frames. A native Windows x64 LFM2 Audio Q8_0 probe passed four real audio decisions with cyclic candidate-order handling. For browser media, either supply evidence bytes in the envelope or use the direct runtime media hook as the playground does. GGUF audio is forwarded when Wllama detects an audio encoder, with media before prompt text. Wllama 3.8.1 reserves workers for audio preprocessing. A real LFM2 Audio probe passed four decisions through the adapter and Rust core in Node/WASM; the corrected browser page still requires a fresh run. The playground offers none , cyclic and balanced ordering for choice questions, including media. Corrections add real model evaluations; none is the default. The local site uses py website/serve.py to set WebAssembly threading headers. Select the llama.cpp runtime and a GGUF model in the playground; the browser loads the model locally from Hugging Face. The samples/build.py web command prepares the TurboJev WASM assets. Troubleshooting If WebGPU is unavailable, select CPU. If initialization runs out of memory, unload the model and try a smaller GGUF quantization. Cancel terminates the worker. Model downloads may take several minutes and require enough browser memory. Generate typed fields Use the same loaded client. The request and response follow the portable workflow contract. fields.js Copy const response = await jev.generate({ context: "Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions: { total: { type: "number", instructions: "What is the total in GBP?" }, overdue: { type: "boolean", instructions: "Is payment overdue?" }, reminder: { type: "string", when: { overdue: true }, depends_on: ["total"], instructions: "Write one short payment reminder.", }, }, thinking: false, text_max_tokens: 128, numeric_max_tokens: 64, }); console.log(response.result, response.skipped, response.usage); The GGUF browser adapter uses JSON Schema grammar for open scalar values. Transformers.js validates bounded greedy output afterward. Neither browser adapter supports thinking; the request above disables it explicitly. Generated enums use their own permutations , independent of load-time orderRobustness . See field capabilities .

title: Android + Swift
text: Android + Swift Both mobile bindings call the C ABI on a dedicated affinity thread. sources ↗ Kotlin Copy val jev = TurboJev.load( JSONObject("{\"model\":\"app/model.gguf\"}") ).join() val request = """{"state":{"message":"My package arrived broken"},"questions":{"department":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which department?","criteria":{"billing":"Payments","shipping":"Delivery"}}}}""" val result = jev.evaluate(JSONObject(request)).join() jev.close() Swift Copy let jev = try TurboJevEngine( optionsJSON: #"{"model":"model.gguf"}"# ) let json = try jev.evaluate(#"{"state":{"message":"My package arrived broken"},"questions":{"department":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which department?","criteria":{"billing":"Payments","shipping":"Delivery"}}}}"#) try jev.close() Generate typed fields Use the same scalar request JSON as the other bindings. Native libraries must be built and packaged for the target platform; Android and Swift are source integrations, not claims of published mobile binaries. Kotlin Copy val fields = JSONObject("""{"context":"Invoice total: 324.50 GBP.","questions":{"total":{"type":"number","instructions":"What is the total in GBP?"}},"thinking":false}""") val response = jev.generate(fields).join() Swift Copy let response = try jev.generate(#"{"context":"Invoice total: 324.50 GBP.","questions":{"total":{"type":"number","instructions":"What is the total in GBP?"}},"thinking":false}"#) These calls belong before the engine close shown above. Native load options, field dependencies, conditions and budgets use the same JSON contract.

title: Option ordering
text: Option ordering Keep the full candidate set visible to the model. Unordered choices and ordered score scales require different treatment: the positions of calm, annoyed, furious define the score; routing keys have no ordinal meaning. Evaluate policies Policy Choice work for K candidates Aggregation none (default) Single pass Ordinary candidate scoring cyclic K caller-order rotations Aligned raw logits averaged before calibration balanced K layouts for even K; 2K for odd K Canonical Williams layouts; calibrate each layout, then average key-aligned probabilities Correction applies only to choice . Mixed requests keep score and noul in an ordinary batch. The corrected core supports up to 32 choice candidates, but a selected runtime can impose a smaller limit. Browser finite scoring supports up to 24. Four choices cost four layouts; three cost six in balanced mode. The result is not recalibrated after averaging. Configure your host Native load JSON Copy { "model": "./model.gguf", "execution": { "orderRobustness": "balanced" } } load.py Copy jev = TurboJev.load("./model.gguf", execution={"orderRobustness": "balanced"}) load.ts Copy const jev = await TurboJev.load({ model: "./model.gguf", execution: { orderRobustness: "balanced" }, }); // Browser: TurboJevWeb.load({...options, orderRobustness: "balanced"}) Load.cs Copy await using var jev = await TurboJevEngine.LoadAsync(new { model = "./model.gguf", execution = new { orderRobustness = "balanced" } }); engine.rs Copy let engine = engine.with_order_robustness(turbojev::OrderRobustness::Balanced); For browser loads, orderRobustness takes precedence over the legacy cyclicOrderRobustness boolean. Native C, Android and Swift use the load JSON above. Exact choice ties select the lexicographically smallest semantic key; enum ties compare JSON value encodings. Unequal probabilities are never treated as ties. Generated enums generate uses per-field permutations instead of the engine policy. auto builds canonical balanced layouts; positive integer budgets sample reproducibly using seed and include the original listing; all scores every permutation, capped at 720. Integer budgets are not generally invariant to caller reorderings. Numeric enums remain unordered; use evaluate with score for ordinal scales. Validation and cost Corrections reduce position sensitivity; they do not establish correct reasoning or calibrated confidence. Fit calibration against the selected policy and measure total latency. In the recorded Windows x64 Qwen3 0.6B Q4_K_M CPU probe, 18/18 routing decisions passed across three cases, three orders and two policies. Balanced distributions had zero keyed drift in that sample; single-pass drift reached 13.7 percentage points. This small sample is not a general accuracy or navigation guarantee. Validation report and reproduction . Corrected responses expose _turbojev.order_robustness and order_evaluations . In default mode the latter is legacy zero, not an inference-call counter. Score training data preserves the scale and varies output codes; regenerate older materialized score data before further training.

title: Decision design
text: Decision design TurboJev executes the requested decision contract. Task accuracy depends on the checkpoint, instructions and evidence. A small model can route a clear message yet fail navigation or coordinate arithmetic. Build the request State the facts needed for the decision; remove redundant prose. Ask one precise question with meaningful candidate keys and distinct descriptions. Keep every candidate visible; use an ordered score only when its sequence defines a real scale. Handle required safety and legality rules in the application, and disclose that policy. Perception and policy A game can expose raw coordinates or derive sensor facts such as nearby obstacles. Disclose derived observations as perception assistance. If a demo claims model-controlled movement, apply the returned direction unchanged and record collisions as failures. A host-computed path or a substituted move must not be counted as an AI decision. Measure quality and speed together Test known answers, failure cases and different candidate orders with the exact model, quantization, device and runtime you will ship. Separate download, load, preprocessing and decision time. Compare none with balanced only when the added evaluations help your task. Thinking generates tokens and adds latency; it is not automatically more accurate. Use evals/run.py for recorded numeric and JevBench evaluations, and scripts/validate-real-option-order.mjs for the real option-order probe. Record request, output, model provenance, errors and latency; never reuse another engine's published scores as TurboJev evidence.

title: Multimodal
text: Multimodal Native llama.cpp and browser llama.cpp/WASM support the portable media envelope when the loaded model, matching projector and runtime build implement that modality. A text GGUF alone does not supply vision or audio. Load a paired GGUF model and projector media.py Copy import base64 from pathlib import Path from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load( "./vision-model.gguf", mmproj="./matching-mmproj.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192, n_seq_max=1 ) as jev: response = jev.evaluate( { "state": { "contract": "turbojev.media.v1", "modality": "image", "base64": base64.b64encode(Path("photo.jpg").read_bytes()).decode("ascii"), }, "questions": { "scene": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "What animal is shown?", "criteria": {"cat": "A cat", "dog": "A dog"}, } }, } ) print(response["answers"]["scene"]) Evidence formats Input Envelope Runtime requirement Image modality: "image", base64 Vision encoder and matching projector Audio modality: "audio", base64 Supported audio model/projector and audio decoding Video frames modality: "video", frames: [{timestamp_ms, base64}] Vision runtime; host decodes frames in timestamp order Optional text provides context alongside media. Video containers must be decoded by the host; TurboJev does not invoke ffmpeg/ffprobe executables. Ordered frames do not prove motion understanding and do not include the audio track. Typed extraction For generate , place the same envelope in context and define scalar fields, such as a receipt total and currency. The response uses result , not answers . Field workflows preserve media bytes while adding dependency answers. Set thinking: false ; native media reasoning and browser reasoning return an explicit unsupported error. Model quality and browser limits The playground offers CLIP/CLAP similarity and LFM2 vision/audio GGUF paths. Similarity models do not follow arbitrary instructions. Browser audio GGUF remains experimental: the recorded Node/WASM adapter probe is not equivalent to qualification in every browser. Downloads, memory and preprocessing can dominate latency. See browser models and limits .

title: Examples
text: Examples Repository samples/ build this checkout. The separate TurboJev.Demos repository uses published packages and CDN assets. Each Python demo owns its implementation and local assets; it does not invoke another demo. Run typed-field samples PowerShell · repository root Copy py samples/build.py native --arch x64 py samples/run.py python --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate py samples/run.py ts --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate py samples/run.py csharp --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate py samples/run.py rust --model C:/models/model.gguf --generate Choose a demo Demo Demonstrates simple Choice, noul and ordered score from one customer message TurboJev-Python Ticket routing and scalar workflow modes fair-die-python Enum distributions and explicit permutation budgets receipt-python / receipt-us-python Image evidence, nullable extraction and dependencies snake-python Model-selected moves, disclosed observations and benchmark output TurboJev-js-native / TurboJev-TS-node / TurboJev-csharp-NET / TurboJev-rust Browser and native host integrations Follow each folder's README for its installation, model and run options. A demo result measures that prompt and model; it is not a guarantee of accuracy for other tasks.

title: Publishing
text: Publishing Registry availability can differ by language. Check the published package and its supported platforms before installing. npm @turbojev/node · @turbojev/web ↗ PyPI turbojev ↗ NuGet TurboJev ↗ crates.io turbojev + modular crates ↗ local release menu Copy pwsh scripts/publish-local.ps1 -Target npm -Yes pwsh scripts/publish-local.ps1 -Target python -Yes pwsh scripts/publish-local.ps1 -Target nuget -Yes pwsh scripts/publish-local.ps1 -Target cargo -Yes pwsh scripts/publish-local.ps1 -Target all -Yes Full notes: docs/LOCAL_PUBLISHING.md ↗ .
